fig1_polar_grid_area.svg: The plane polar / cylindrical grid from `cyl_to_cart`: circles $\rho=$const and rays $\phi=$const. The area element is $dA=\rho\,d\rho\,d\phi$ (the Jacobian `cyl_jacobian`$=\rho$), so for equal $\Delta\rho,\Delta\phi$ the outer cell (orange, $\rho\approx2.75$) has about 3.7 times the area of the inner one (blue, $\rho\approx0.75$) -- the area grows in proportion to $\rho$.
fig2_spherical_frame.svg: The spherical moving frame from `sph_basis`. At a point $P(r,\theta,\phi)$ the orthonormal right-handed triad $(\hat e_r,\hat e_\theta,\hat e_\phi)$ is tangent to the coordinate curves: $\hat e_r$ along the radius, $\hat e_\theta$ along the meridian ($\phi$ fixed, orange), $\hat e_\phi$ along the parallel ($\theta$ fixed, purple). Unlike fixed Cartesian axes, the basis depends on position.
